_comment: The bound graded operating point. Every field here is FROZEN. A recipe that names any of these keys is a frozen-axis write and is recorded as one.
_vocab_size_note: the real corpus's vocabulary. The shards carry GPT-2 BPE ids, 50257 of them, and the embedding is padded to 50304 to keep the last dimension a multiple of 128. This is the same number the production track3nov runner freezes at frozen_defs.py:226. It is NOT a free choice: a smaller table cannot index the corpus.
_rescale_note: Rescaled from 12 layers / 768 dim / 524288 tokens per step / 3600 steps to fit fifty graded refinement iterations inside the six-hour session bound. Layers halve, width halves and the batch quarters, so the per-step cost falls by roughly 4x from width, 2x from depth and 4x from batch. THE CEILING IS NOW 2000, DOWN FROM 3000, AND THAT CUT IS A MEASUREMENT. MEASURED 2026-08-31 on one H100 in bf16 through tests/train_eval.py at this exact operating point: 0.155 to 0.166 s/step across four optimizer families, so 2000 steps costs 311 to 332 s against the 432 s per-attempt bound and 3000 steps would cost 466 to 498 s and bust it. A ceiling an attempt cannot reach is not a ceiling, it is a trap: it was also the DEFAULT for a recipe that omits max_steps, so an omission alone exceeded the budget.
_target_loss_note: STALE. 3.28 was anchored against the 12-layer / 768-dim / 524288-token substrate. A 6-layer / 384-dim model on a quarter of the batch is a far weaker model on real text and there is no evidence it reaches 3.28 at any step, so this bar may now be uncrossable. Re-measure before grading. Deliberately left at the old value rather than replaced with a guess.
dataset: fineweb10B, real corpus, mounted by the pinned task image at /workspace/data/fineweb10B
_dataset_note: 20 train shards of 100000000 GPT-2 BPE tokens plus one held-out shard of the same size, uint16 after a 256-int32 header whose magic is 20240520. The synthetic first-order Markov source this replaced, whose transition table WAS the dataset and was seeded by data_seed_dist 20260101, is gone; the data_seed_dist key is gone with it because there is no distribution left to seed.
data_draw_val: verifier-only, never present on the agent surface
_data_draw_note: A draw now selects which window of a split's own region of the corpus is read, not a random realisation. train reads the train shards; dev reads the first half of the held-out shard; val reads the second half. dev and val are disjoint by the shard layout rather than by the secrecy of a seed, so the held-out split stays held out even if the graded draw leaks.
_stream_tokens_note: stream_tokens_train was 268435456 tokens of generated stream; it is now exactly one shard of real text, which is the largest round window that stays well inside memory once widened to int64. At 131072 tokens per step over 2000 steps the loop draws about 262 million tokens of batches from this 100 million token pool, so it revisits it roughly 2.6 times. The dev and val windows are unchanged at 4194304 and each fits its half of the held-out shard about 11 times over.
operating_point_state: unmeasured on the bound envelope, carried under gap-oer-scaled-operating-point-unmeasured. The rescale above did not close this gap and did not narrow it: it moved the operating point again, so target_loss and the score anchors are now stale against a substrate nobody has timed or scored.
